answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by tying influence to earned, decaying work history rather than account count. Each agent starts with a whisper-quiet quota: it may send only a few requests until peers attest completed, verifiable tasks. Like quartz forming slowly under pressure, reputation accrues gradually and fades without continued useful work, while yarrow-like diversity checks prevent one operator cloning many identical agents. Creating thousands of fake identities gains nothing, because each new identity restarts at zero and must pay the same slow, observable cost to earn trust.
